h1: AI agents and automations for Stripe
answer: To put Stripe to work in 50agents, connect it once and tell Captain the job, such as “when a customer subscribes in Stripe, post it in a Slack channel”.

Captain builds an automation that fires on Stripe events such as a payment, refund, failed payment or new subscription, or an AI agent that reads your payments and writes you a summary of what changed.

faqs.q: Can it tell me when a payment fails?
faqs.a: Yes. “Payment Fails” starts an automation when Stripe reports it, so it can post in Slack or add the customer to a follow-up list. Emailing the customer about it waits for your approval.

faqs.q: Will it refund or charge customers on its own?
faqs.a: No. Anything that spends or moves money asks you first in Needs you. An action like “Collect Payment” runs only after your yes.

faqs.q: Can it log refunds as well as payments?
faqs.a: Yes. “Charge Refunded” and “New Refund Created” are separate triggers, so refunds can go to their own rows or their own tab in the same sheet.

faqs.q: How is this different from Stripe’s own AI tools?
faqs.a: Stripe’s pages on AI agents are written for developers: an MCP server, plugins and tools for selling through AI agents. 50agents is for the person who owns the Stripe account, who describes the job while Captain builds it without code. If your developers are building your own AI product on Stripe, Stripe’s tools are the direct route.
